a lot

It's...okay? It's better than made up words, but the trick is that those words together don't inherently mean anything. So unless you
make
them mean something in the story of your game, it can be a negative factor in people's evaluations of your project.

Gunmetal_Dreams said:

Click to expand...
So my comment actually wasn't about the filing cabinets, it was about the desks and counters. I agree that the bottom tile of the filing cabinets should be on the floor, not the wall.
But to my eye, having the top tile of the desks end before the wall makes it look like they are not against the wall, which is where you'd typically expect the desks to be in an office.
I know it's not the same pieces of furniture, but see your desks compared to this:
To me, that perspective looks better. If you were actually, like, on a ladder against the south wall and looking at furniture against the north wall, you wouldn't be able to see the bottom of that wall, right?
But it's a matter of taste - there's no official rule saying "you have to place your pixel furniture in this position or it's wrong"
I'm just offering the feedback based on my preference.

That sounds like you might either be using the wrong tiles for the walls/floor/ceiling or you're placing the furniture in a way that breaks the autotiling of the walls.
It is intended that if the character has access to the ceiling tiles, they can walk through them - that's so that you can have different elevations on a map.
In order to achieve the effect I showed you in my screenshot, I had to use shift-right click and shift-click to copy the desk autotiles without changing the wall autotiles.
